{"choices":[{"finish_reason":"tool_calls","index":0,"message":{"content":"The implementation looks good. Let me summarize the changes I made:

## Summary

The issue was that `Style/SoleNestedConditional` did not maintain operator precedence when auto-correcting a negated nested conditional (`unless`) whose condition was a comparison method (like `===`, `==`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`) called without parentheses.

### Root Cause

In Ruby, the `!` (boolean NOT) operator binds **tighter** than comparison operators. So `!t === value.public_send(a)` is parsed as `(!t) === value.public_send(a)` rather than `!(t === value.public_send(a))`.

When merging a nested `unless t === value.public_send(a)` into the outer condition, the cop:
1. Prepended `!` via the `&& !` operator (or `!` prefix).
2. Parenthesized the **arguments** of the comparison method (producing `t ===(value.public_send(a))`) instead of wrapping the **whole** comparison expression.

This resulted in `!t ===(value.public_send(a))` â semantically wrong.

### Fix

I modified `replace_condition` and `wrap_condition` to accept a `negated:` keyword argument. When the condition is negated (`unless`) **and** is a comparison method that is not parenthesized, the whole expression is wrapped in parentheses `(condition)` instead of parenthesizing just the arguments. Combined with the prepended `!`, this produces `!(t === value.public_send(a))`, preserving the original semantics.

The three call sites that build the merged condition were updated to pass the negation status:
- `correct_for_guard_condition_style` (modifier form, e.g. `do_something unless t === ...`)
- `correct_for_basic_condition_style` (basic form, e.g. `unless t === ...; ...; end`)
- `correct_for_outer_condition_modify_form_style` (outer modifier form, e.g. `if foo; ...; end unless t === ...`)

### Behavior preserved
- Non-negated comparison conditions are unchanged (arguments still get parenthesized, e.g. `t ===(value.public_send(a))`).
- Non-comparison method calls (e.g. `foo.is_a? Foo`) are unchanged (`!foo.is_a?(Foo)` is correct since method calls bind tighter than `!`).
- `and_type`/`or_type` conditions are unchanged.
- Already-parenthesized comparison conditions work correctly.

This fix also enables proper interaction with `Style/InverseMethods`, which can now correctly invert `!(t == value)` into `t != value`.
